data.claim: About 80 percent exists or is planned in P-schedule (job model and trigger model done; due, run, author, defaults, emitters, executor, backpressure, escalation, inbox, org layers open). Missing: (1) automatic evaluation of event triggers (trigger evaluate is called only by an unreachable CLI verb), (2) a facts catalogue with churn (lines changed since last run), (3) a condition predicate on a job, (4) every_lines cadence, (5) check/notify action kinds, (6) per-job limits and run keys beyond B-sched-backpressure, (7) container execution of job actions via lane transport, (8) company-policy jobs with user override, (9) a security review of the job surface, (10) churn/surface/docs-drift job templates. Recommend NO daemon: evaluate lazily at brief, session start, merge, complete and loop ticks, plus one bounded idempotent 'schedule tick' for external cron, systemd, Actions or routines (already D-sched-no-daemon-r2).
data.falsifier: A job whose trigger is churn >= N lines fires without N lines changed, fires twice for the same sha (run key), or an agent-created job runs without operator enablement or bypasses an approval.
data.mechanism: Due and fire state are derived from the event log (calendar days, done tasks, done phases, and a new churn fact computed by git numstat since the sha stored in the last cadence.ran). A job is a definition (schedule record) with triggers, an optional 'when' predicate over derived facts (all/any clauses of fact, op, value; no eval), an action that files items or runs a read-only check, limits and layer. Triggers file queue items only (D-trigger-actions-create-items); agents start only through the lane launcher (D-sched-no-daemon-r2). Best practice mapping: K8s concurrencyPolicy Forbid and startingDeadlineSeconds map to concurrency_group and missed skip|once; GitHub Actions schedule is delayed, runs only on default branch and auto-disables after 60 days idle so ddflow must detect silent no-fire; Renovate prHourlyLimit/prConcurrentLimit map to open-item caps and hourly cap; SonarQube new-code conditions (new-code coverage >=80, duplication <=3 percent) justify thresholds on NEW code, i.e. churn-triggered rather than whole-repo; Claude Code routines have a one-hour minimum, schedule, API and GitHub triggers, fresh session per run, daily caps: ddflow keeps due-state in its own log so it works with any of them.
data.probe: ddflow cadence; ddflow task list --phase P-schedule; grep callers of triggers.evaluate and add_schedule_parser; decisions D-sched-no-daemon-r2, D-sched-triggers-separate, D-trigger-actions-create-items, D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06

data.question: Can ddflow run time-, event- and threshold-triggered jobs with validation predicates, per project/company/user, for audits, churn-triggered reviews, dependency upgrades, main-red repair, goals checks, container runs? What exists, what is planned, what is missing?

data.body: SIZE S, RISK low. Extend Schedule (core/records/content.py) and SCHEDULE_FIELDS with: triggers (list of {kind: time|event|threshold, ...}), when (predicate clauses, see SJ-when), action ({kind: file_item|check|notify|bug|note, template}), layer (default|company|project|local|user, derived from where the TOML lives, never user-set in an event), locked (company policy: user may disable only if allowed), owner. Old definitions fold unchanged (defaults). Unknown field refused (fail closed), validated before write, recorded as an amendment. Acceptance: round-trip of an old and a new definition through fold and replay; unknown or out-of-range value refused; a definition from an agent cannot set enabled=true or layer (SJ-job-security). Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Job schema extension: triggers list, when predicate, action kind, layer, locked, owner, limits fields with validation

data.body: SIZE M, RISK med. A registry of named, pure, derived facts (r-derive-dont-store: none stored): churn_lines(since=last_run|sha|days, globs) via git numstat against the sha recorded in the last cadence.ran or schedule run (reuse services/changes.py ChangeDetector, B-uni-git-queries); files_touched(globs); main_red (last ci.result on main); open_bugs(globs); queue_idle; advisories_new (SEC-deps when landed, else unavailable); age_days(job). A fact that cannot be computed returns UNAVAILABLE, never 0 or false (r-unavailable-not-pass). Bounded cost: git calls capped and cached per evaluation. Acceptance: churn counts added+deleted lines excluding lockfiles and generated paths (configurable list); same sha gives same value; git failure gives UNAVAILABLE. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Derived project facts for job conditions: churn (lines changed since last run), files touching globs, main_red, open bugs, queue idle, advisories, due age

data.body: SIZE S, RISK low. Operator example: 'we created 500 new lines of code, run an extra bug assessment'. Adds the threshold trigger kind {fact, op, value, min_interval, cooldown} and the every_lines cadence next to every_days, every_tasks and every_phases, evaluated inside B-sched-due's due computation; run key = job + head sha + threshold so an unchanged tree never re-fires; knob [schedule_jobs].default_churn_lines. Acceptance with a fake repo: 499 lines no fire, 500 fires once, a second evaluation at the same sha is a no-op, the counter restarts from the run's sha. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. data.body: SIZE M, RISK med. The validation rule of a job: when = {all|any: [{fact, op(<,<=,==,>=,>,in), value}]}, plus not. Pure function over SJ-facts, no expression language, no eval, no shell (OPA/Cedar-style data, not code). UNAVAILABLE fact makes the whole condition unavailable and the job reports it rather than firing or passing silently. Every evaluation, including false, is a logged event with the fact values (audit, like trigger.evaluated). Reuse services/approvals/policy.py predicate conventions rather than a second matcher; check guidance engine for a shared matcher first and say what was reused. Acceptance: truth table, nested all/any, unavailable propagation, malformed predicate refused at definition time. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Condition predicate for jobs: declarative all/any clauses over derived facts, evaluated without eval, reusing the approvals policy predicate shape

data.body: SIZE M, RISK med. Found by R-scheduler-2026-11-11: triggers.evaluate is reachable only from api.schedule.trigger_evaluate and nothing calls it automatically. This task is the single entry point: tick(now) evaluates due schedules (B-sched-due) and event triggers (B-trigger-model), files items, writes trigger.evaluated, under a lock with a time budget and the global hourly cap; callers: brief, session start, after worktree.merged and item completion, loop ticks, and the CLI/MCP verb 'schedule tick' for external schedulers (B-sched-emitters prints the line that runs it; ADP-scheduler registers it). No daemon. Concurrent ticks collapse to one (lease on the tick). Acceptance: two ticks at once file once; a tick after 10 days of outage files once per job (missed policy), no storm; a tick on a clean repo costs no git call beyond the facts requested. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Lazy evaluation of triggers and due jobs: at brief, session start, merge and complete, plus one bounded idempotent 'schedule tick' for external cron, systemd, Actions or routines

data.body: SIZE M, RISK high. B-sched-run files items; this adds the other action kinds without a new execution path: check = a command from the allow-listed [schedule_jobs].check_commands run through cmdrunner with a timeout and output cap, outcome ok|findings|failed|unavailable recorded as schedule.run evidence (never an agent, never writes the tree); bug = ddflow bug found with dedupe key; notify = through the notify port with owner, next call and dedupe key (r-alert-owner-next-call); note = session note. Spawning an agent run stays with the lane launcher and D-dispatch-modes: the action files a kind=job item and the executor (P-schedule.unattended) may dispatch it. Open question for the operator: may a check run mutating commands? Default no. Acceptance: each kind has a failing-first test; a check that times out is unavailable; command not on the allow-list refused. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Job action kinds: file item from template (extend B-sched-run), read-only check command with recorded evidence, notify, open bug, record note

data.body: SIZE M, RISK low. Consume B-sched-backpressure (open cap, decline memory, breaker, kill switch); do not add a second breaker. Adds what it lacks: limits {max_runs_per_window, window, backoff_base, backoff_max, budget_tokens, budget_usd} per job, exponential backoff with jitter after a failed or unavailable run (K8s startingDeadlineSeconds and Renovate hourly limits as the models), run key = job + sha + threshold hash, concurrency_group Forbid semantics (skip while the previous run is open). Budget numbers come from P-governor when it lands; until then count items and turns (existing budget field). A stop is a recorded event and a needs_operator notice, never silent. Acceptance: window cap, backoff doubling and ceiling, jitter bounded, Forbid skip, stop visible in brief. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Job limits: max runs per window, run-key idempotency, backoff with jitter after failure, token or cost budget per run and per window, visible stop

data.body: SIZE M, RISK low. TOML plus jinja prompt per job, each declaring trigger, when, action, limits, container yes/no, approval needed. Threshold-driven: churn-bug-assessment (500 lines), churn-dedupe (500 lines, dedupe sweep scoped to touched globs), docs-drift (docs changed less than code). Event-driven: debug-main-red (ci.failed on main; bisect via DBG-commit-bisect; overlaps B-trigger-defaults ci.failed so it only adds the diagnosis lens and references that trigger). data.body: SIZE S, RISK low. Items a job files (fix mode, check findings, bugs) carry tags origin:job and schedule:<id>, a priority band below operator work, no needs onto in-flight tasks and declared literal globs, so a job never stalls the queue or a running lane; placement uses the plan lint and optimizer port (P-optimizer) when present; expiry to a report reuses B-sched-escalation. data.summary: B-sched-model and B-trigger-model are done, but ddflow/surfaces/commands/schedule.py add_schedule_parser is imported only by tests; 'ddflow schedule list' gives 'invalid choice' in 0.2.11 and nothing calls api.schedule.trigger_evaluate, so defined triggers are never evaluated. Regression test: the CLI parser accepts 'schedule list' and 'schedule trigger evaluate --dry-run'. Related: SJ-tick, B-sched-author.

data.body: SIZE M, RISK high. Jobs are a privilege-escalation path. Threat model and enforced checks: (1) an agent-proposed job, trigger or watch starts disabled and only a person enables it (D-sched-triggers-separate); (2) editing a job definition is a guarded config change (services/approvals/config_guard.py); (3) a job acts with its recorded class, never the creator's or a session's authority; actions touching dependencies, security, architecture, outward effects need approval each time unless a recorded standing consent exists (r-consent-outward, standing approval window); (4) check commands only from the allow-list, no shell interpolation of fact or record text (r-untrusted-data); (5) a company locked job cannot be weakened by project files; (6) hop limit and breaker still bind job-created items. Acceptance: one failing-first test per attack (agent sets enabled, template sets layer, record text injected into a command, job files a task that edits its own definition, job loop via its own failure). Independent cross-family review required. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.
data.title: Security review and tests of the job surface: no job, trigger or template can bypass approvals or enable itself

data.body: SIZE M, RISK med. A job's execution target is data (job.exec = local|container|ssh|dsh), resolved by ADP-lane-transport (done). Container: image from config, repo mounted read-only unless mode=fix, no network unless the job declares hosts, cpu/memory/time caps, output capped, cleanup always. Used by check actions (SJ-actions) and by agent runs the executor dispatches. A runtime that is missing is recorded unavailable, never passed (r-unavailable-not-pass); fake adapter for tests. Acceptance: read-only mount enforced, timeout kills and cleans, missing runtime unavailable, same result through local and container fake. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

data.body: SIZE M, RISK med. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Jobs layer by D-config-layer-order and D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06: a job id in a higher layer replaces the lower definition field by field; company policy jobs carry locked=true|false (locked: a user override must be an explicit, recorded, person-only act, never agent-made); a new company job starts in audit mode (reports what it would file) for one release (D-GP-Q5); schedule show names each layer and origin. Until B-org-layers lands, project, local and user layers already work through SJ-fields. Acceptance: precedence matrix, locked override requires a person, audit mode files nothing. Bounded, literal globs.
